logline: A former special forces soldier drives a vigilante taxi service that delivers justice - and revenge - to victims whose perpetrators walked free.

renewal.note: Three seasons completed (2021, 2023, 2025-2026). Season 3 finale drew 16.6% - SBS history-maker. Season 4 unconfirmed as of June 2026.

bollymeter.basis: IMDb 8.1; AsianWiki 96/100 (7,843 votes); audience consensus centres on Lee Je-hoon's controlled performance and the show's willingness to take its vigilante premise seriously as social commentary rather than pure action.

pull_quotes.text: A vigilante thriller with a social conscience - each case is drawn from real Korean crimes, which keeps the action from feeling like fantasy.

seasons.review_body: Taxi Driver operates on a formula - victim, crime, covert operation, resolution - but the formula works because the cases are rooted in documented Korean social failures: cult exploitation, workplace abuse, school violence. That grounding is what separates it from the vigilante genre's usual wish-fulfillment mechanics. Lee Je-hoon carries the show with a performance calibrated precisely for the genre: enough warmth to maintain audience sympathy, enough cold control to make the vengeance credible. The supporting team is sketched in quickly and effectively. The show's finale became the fourth highest-rated Friday-Saturday drama in SBS history. Critics praised its case selection; those who wanted deeper character excavation found the procedural structure limiting.

episode_reviews.title: The Taxi Driver
episode_reviews.review_body: Taxi Driver Season 1 Episode 1 'The Taxi Driver' aired April 9, 2021 on SBS as the premiere of the 16-episode first season. IMDb audience scored the season 8.1. The RT consensus called it 'a vigilante thriller with a social conscience - each case is drawn from real Korean crimes, which keeps the action from feeling like fantasy.' The premiere establishes Kim Do-gi's backstory and the Rainbow Taxi Company's clandestine operation with efficient, confident storytelling: cases rooted in documented Korean social failures, a protagonist with enough controlled darkness to make the vigilante logic credible, and a visual grammar that reveals the taxi's interior reconfigurations as the episode's thesis statement. Lee Je-hoon establishes Do-gi with the stillness of a performance calibrated precisely for the genre: enough warmth to maintain sympathy, enough cold control to make the vengeance credible. The show makes its pitch in one episode and commits completely.
episode_reviews.spoiler_free: The opener establishes Kim Do-gi's backstory and the taxi company's clandestine operation with efficient, confident storytelling. The first case begins immediately; the show has no interest in slow burns - its proposition is clear by the twenty-minute mark and it commits completely.
episode_reviews.the_moment: The moment the taxi's interior reconfigurations are revealed - the show's visual thesis statement.

critic_note.text: A genre pilot that sets up its premise and pays it off in the same episode.

bollymeter.basis: IMDb consistent with Season 1; audience response indicates the format holds but the cases feel slightly less fresh than the first run; production quality maintained.

seasons.review_body: Season 2 delivers the same vigilante case-of-the-arc structure with consistent craft. The cases are still socially anchored and Lee Je-hoon is still doing exactly what he needs to do. The criticism is not that the show deteriorated but that the formula is now entirely legible - the audience knows when the reveal will come and what shape the resolution will take. Those who came for the cases stay loyal; those who wanted evolution found it incremental. The ensemble gets more to do than in Season 1, which helps.
seasons.season_over_season: Consistent with Season 1 in execution; the format is fully exposed, which is its ceiling.

bollymeter.basis: 16.6% finale rating - series peak and SBS historic high; audience returned in larger numbers than any previous season, suggesting the show found a way to re-energise the format in the final run.

seasons.review_body: Season 3 turned out to be the series' commercial apex. The 16.6% finale rating is extraordinary for a franchise in its third run; the audience response suggested the cases in this season hit with renewed relevance. The ending left the door open for a fourth season, which as of June 2026 has not been officially confirmed despite strong fan demand and positive cast statements. A fitting conclusion to a run that got better, dipped, then found a high note.
seasons.season_over_season: The strongest commercial performance of the three seasons; whether it is artistically the peak is debated.
